title: DocumentReference → note
notes:
DocumentReference carries unstructured/residual clinical content (a progress note, discharge summary, …) that has no structured OMOP home. Per f2o-081 it is routed to the `note` table rather than discarded. One DocumentReference with a text attachment → one note row.

Stage 1 (`mapspec/views/DocumentReference__note.view.json`) flattens: `type.coding[LOINC]` → note_class_concept_id, `content.first().attachment.data` (base64) → note_text, `subject` → person_id, `context.encounter.first()` → visit, `date` → note_date, `author[Practitioner]` → provider. Stage 2 (`mapspec/etl/DocumentReference__note.sql`) base64-decodes the attachment, resolves the LOINC document-type to a Standard concept (LEFT JOIN, 0 if none), and — because DocumentReference.date is optional while note_date is NOT NULL in v5.4 — falls back to the linked Encounter.period.start via staging.encounter_visit (same cross-resource date pattern as Condition). note_type_concept_id 32817 'EHR', encoding 32678 'UTF-8', language 4180186 'English'. Status filter drops entered-in-error/superseded. A DocumentReference with no decodable text and no date is dropped (no silent empty note).

cases.desc: (a) their F2O connectathon shape: DocumentReference with LOINC 11506-3 'Progress note', a text/plain base64 attachment, subject + context.encounter but NO date → one note row; note_text = base64-decoded content, note_date falls back to Encounter.period.start (f2o-081 residual-content routing)

note.note_text: Patient reports improved breathing since starting inhaler.
